offering_description.value: Palomar is a specialty property and casualty insurer that underwrites catastrophe-exposed and niche risks such as earthquake, flood, wind, hurricane, inland marine, fronting and crop coverage. It sells mainly through wholesale brokers, retail agents and program partners to homeowners, businesses and other insureds, and uses reinsurance to manage its risk.

primary_products.value: earthquake insurance; residential flood insurance; commercial property and inland marine insurance; hurricane and wind insurance; casualty and crop insurance

primary_services.value: insurance underwriting; fronting services for program partners; reinsurance placement

customer_segment.value: B2C: homeowners and renters buying earthquake, flood and hurricane coverage; B2B: commercial property owners, businesses, contractors and program partners buying specialty coverage

end_markets.value: residential property insurance; commercial property insurance; inland marine; agriculture; specialty casualty

revenue_model.value: interest or premiums: insurance premiums written and earned, plus investment income on the insurance float; commissions or management fees: fronting fees and ceding commissions from program and reinsurance arrangements
revenue_model.category: interest or premiums; commissions or management fees

value_chain_position.value: financial intermediary: underwrites and carries specialty insurance risk, cedes part to reinsurers, and sells via brokers and agents to policyholders

geography_served.value: US national: Admitted and surplus lines coverage across most US states, with strong California and coastal exposures

specialization.value: related lines: catastrophe-exposed property, inland marine, casualty, fronting and crop insurance lines

distribution_channels.value: agents / brokers: wholesale brokers, retail agents and managing general agents; partners / resellers: program partners and fronting relationships

regulatory_exposure.value: high: Licensed insurer regulated by state insurance departments on rates, solvency and surplus lines rules
